questions.q: What is the primary function of xylem tissue in flowering plants?
a: Transporting water and dissolved mineral ions from roots to leaves
Transporting manufactured sugars and amino acids
Storing starch grains in root tubers
Performing active photosynthesis

questions.q: Which tissue in plants is responsible for the translocation of sucrose and amino acids?
a: Xylem vessels
Phloem tissue
Cortex parenchyma
Waxy cuticle

questions.q: What is transpiration defined as?
a: The active uptake of water by root hairs
The movement of sugars from source to sink
The evaporation of water at the surfaces of the mesophyll cells followed by the loss of water vapor from plant leaves through the stomata
The condensation of water inside stem vessels

questions.q: Which of the following environmental factors typically increases the rate of transpiration?
a: High humidity
Still, windless air
Low temperatures
High temperature, low humidity, and increased air movement (wind)

questions.q: How does increased humidity affect the rate of transpiration?
a: It decreases the rate of transpiration by reducing the water potential gradient between the air spaces inside the leaf and the external air
It increases the rate significantly
It has no effect on water vapor loss
It forces stomata to open wider

questions.q: What is the role of root hairs in water uptake?
a: To secrete digestive enzymes into the soil
To provide a large surface area for the absorption of water by osmosis and mineral ions by active transport
To transport sugars downward
To anchor the plant against strong winds

questions.q: What path does water take as it moves across a root from the soil to the xylem?
a: Phloem -> Cortex -> Stomata -> Epidermis
Xylem -> Root hair -> Stem -> Leaf
Root hair cell -> Root cortex cells -> Xylem vessels
Stomata -> Mesophyll -> Root cortex

questions.q: What term describes a plant losing water vapor faster than it can absorb replacement water, causing cells to lose turgor?
a: Translocation
Guttation
Osmosis
Wilting

questions.q: Which instrument is commonly used to measure the rate of transpiration (water uptake) in a leafy shoot?
a: Potometer
Barometer
Calorimeter
Respirometer

questions.q: Why are xylem vessel walls strengthened with a tough, waterproof substance called lignin?
a: To store food reserves
To prevent xylem vessels from collapsing under the negative pressure created by transpiration pull and to provide structural support
To allow active transport of sugars
To trap sunlight for photosynthesis

questions.q: What is meant by the term 'translocation' in plant biology?
a: The evaporation of water from leaves
The movement of water up xylem vessels
The movement of sucrose and amino acids through phloem from sources to sinks
The diffusion of carbon dioxide into stomata

questions.q: What is a 'source' in the context of phloem transport?
a: A region where sugars are consumed or stored, such as roots or growing fruits
An area where water enters root hairs
A leaf cell performing respiration
A part of the plant that releases or produces sugars, such as mature leaves photosynthesizing

questions.q: What is a 'sink' in plant transport systems?
a: A region of the plant where sucrose and amino acids are stored or used (e.g., growing roots, tubers, or developing flowers)
A region where water evaporates into the atmosphere
A pool of water in the soil
A storage vacuole inside a guard cell

questions.q: How do root hair cells absorb mineral ions when their concentration in the soil is lower than inside the cell sap?
a: By simple diffusion down a concentration gradient
By active transport, utilizing energy (ATP) from respiration to move ions against the concentration gradient
By osmosis through partially permeable membranes
By bulk flow driven by transpiration pull

questions.q: Which of the following features distinguishes xylem vessels from phloem sieve tubes?
a: Xylem consists of living cells with companion cells
Phloem transports water and mineral ions upward
Xylem vessels are composed of dead, hollow, lignified cells joined end-to-end with no end walls
Phloem contains thick rings of lignin

questions.q: What structural feature of phloem sieve tubes allows the movement of organic solutes?
a: Thick woody walls made of cellulose and lignin
Dead hollow tubes with spiral thickening
Completely blocked end plates
Sieve plates with pores that allow the flow of sap, supported by adjacent companion cells

questions.q: What is the primary driving force that pulls water up through the xylem vessels from the roots to the leaves?
a: Transpiration pull (creating a water potential gradient and suction pressure)
Active pumping by root cells
Root pressure alone
Gravity pulling water downward

questions.q: Why does an increase in wind speed increase the rate of transpiration?
a: It cools down the plant leaves instantly
It blows away water vapor accumulating around the stomata, maintaining a steep concentration gradient for diffusion
It forces stomata to close tightly
It increases humidity around the leaf

questions.q: Which of the following adaptations would you expect to find in xerophytes (plants adapted to arid, dry environments) to reduce water loss?
a: Broad, thin leaves with numerous open stomata on the upper surface
Absence of any root system
Rolled leaves, sunken stomata, thick waxy cuticles, and reduced leaf surface area (e.g., spines)
Large permanent vacuoles filled with air

questions.q: What role do companion cells play next to phloem sieve tube elements?
a: They provide structural support using lignin rings
They transport water up from the roots
They carry out photosynthesis in the dark
They provide metabolic energy and control the loading and unloading of sugars into the sieve tubes

questions.q: How does temperature affect the rate of transpiration?
a: Higher temperatures increase kinetic energy and evaporation rates, speeding up transpiration
Higher temperatures freeze water inside the stem
Temperature has no effect on water loss
Higher temperatures cause stomata to seal permanently

questions.q: What happens to a plant shoot in a potometer experiment if the surrounding air temperature rises significantly and a fan is turned on?
a: The air bubble in the capillary tube stops moving completely
The rate of water uptake (bubble movement) increases rapidly
Water flows backward into the reservoir
The plant absorbs water through its leaves

questions.q: Which of the following correctly describes the distribution of xylem and phloem in a dicotyledonous root?
a: Vascular bundles arranged in a ring near the outer edge
Xylem scattered randomly through the cortex
Xylem typically arranged in a central star shape or solid core, with phloem situated between the arms
Phloem located in the exact center surrounded by a thick waxy ring

questions.q: How are vascular bundles arranged in the stem of a herbaceous dicotyledonous plant?
a: Randomly scattered throughout the stem diameter
Concentrated entirely in the center like a solid rod
Forming an inner ring of phloem and outer ring of xylem
Forming a ring near the outer edge of the stem

questions.q: What is the main function of companion cells in phloem tissue?
a: To actively load and unload sugars into sieve tubes using ATP energy
To transport water and mineral salts
To provide rigid mechanical support
To generate root pressure

questions.q: Which direction does transport occur within xylem vessels?
a: Downward from leaves to roots only
Upward only, from roots to stem and leaves
In both upward and downward directions simultaneously
Horizontally across cortex cells only

questions.q: Unlike xylem, what is a key characteristic regarding the direction of transport in phloem tissue?
a: Transport occurs exclusively downward from leaves
Transport occurs exclusively upward from roots
Transport can occur in both directions (upward and downward) from sources to sinks depending on the plant's needs and season
Transport stops completely at night

questions.q: What is the primary purpose of the waxy cuticle covering plant leaves in relation to transport?
a: To absorb sunlight for photosynthesis
To allow carbon dioxide to enter freely
To transport mineral ions
To minimize uncontrolled water loss by evaporation from the leaf surface

questions.q: Why do plants wilt when the rate of transpiration exceeds the rate of water absorption by the roots?
a: Cells lose turgor pressure as vacuoles shrink, making plant tissues limp
Xylem vessels dissolve in acid
Phloem tubes burst from excess pressure
Stomata open too wide

questions.q: What experimental precaution is essential when setting up a potometer to measure transpiration accurately?
a: The shoot must be cut under water to prevent air bubbles from entering and blocking the xylem vessels
The leaves must be coated in petroleum jelly
The plant must be kept in complete darkness for a week
The roots must be removed entirely

questions.q: What is root pressure?
a: The negative suction pressure created by leaf evaporation
The physical weight of the soil pressing on roots
A pressure generated in the roots by active transport of mineral ions into xylem, pushing water a short distance upward
The pressure of sucrose moving through phloem

questions.q: Which of the following cells are dead at maturity?
a: Palisade mesophyll cells
Root hair cells
Phloem sieve tube elements
Xylem vessel elements

questions.q: What happens to stomata during periods of severe drought or water stress to protect the plant?
a: Guard cells lose turgor and close the stomata, significantly reducing transpiration water loss
Stomata open wider to let cool air in
Stomata dissolve completely
Leaves drop all their chloroplasts

questions.q: What is the primary substance transported in xylem vessels?
a: Sucrose solution
Water and dissolved mineral ions (such as nitrates, magnesium, and phosphates)
Molten starch
Amino acid solutions

questions.q: Which of the following best explains how water molecules stay bonded together as they are pulled up xylem vessels?
a: Active transport by companion cells
Cohesion (hydrogen bonding between water molecules) and adhesion to xylem walls
Osmotic pressure from root hairs
Centrifugal force from stem rotation

questions.q: What is the function of pits found in the lignified walls of xylem vessels?
a: To allow gas exchange with air spaces
To secrete digestive enzymes
To let sugars diffuse into the phloem
To allow lateral movement of water and mineral ions between adjacent vessels

questions.q: Which plant organs act as 'sources' during the spring season when new leaves begin to grow from stored reserves?
a: Storage organs like root tubers or bulbs
Mature flowers
Developing seeds
The soil surrounding the roots

questions.q: What causes the movement of liquid in a capillary tube potometer during measurement?
a: Photosynthesis producing oxygen gas
Water uptake by the leafy shoot to replace water lost through transpiration
Active pumping by root cells
Evaporation from the glass tubing reservoir

questions.q: How does high light intensity affect transpiration rate during the daytime?
a: It causes stomata to close immediately
It has no effect on water loss
It causes stomata to open wide for gas exchange, increasing light absorption and raising the rate of transpiration
It freezes water inside the leaf

questions.q: Which of the following structures is absent in mature phloem sieve tube elements?
a: Cell membrane
Cytoplasm strands
Cellulose cell wall
A nucleus
